title: Understanding Diffusion Models: A Unified Perspective

nodes.text: Diffusion models have both likelihood-based and score-based interpretations, and this work reviews them under a unified perspective deriving the underlying mathematics in detail.
nodes.evidence: we explore and review diffusion models, which as we will demonstrate, have both likelihood-based and score-based interpretations.

nodes.text: A Variational Diffusion Model (VDM) can be understood as a Markovian Hierarchical Variational Autoencoder (MHVAE) with three restrictions: latent dimension equals data dimension, the encoder at each step is a fixed (non-learned) linear Gaussian, and the final-timestep latent distribution is a standard Gaussian.
nodes.evidence: The easiest way to think of a Variational Diffusion Model (VDM) ... is simply as a Markovian Hierarchical Variational Autoencoder with three key restrictions

nodes.text: The evidence equals the ELBO plus the KL divergence between the approximate posterior q(z|x) and the true posterior p(z|x); since this KL is non-negative, maximizing the ELBO necessarily minimizes the gap to the true posterior.
nodes.evidence: the evidence is equal to the ELBO plus the KL Divergence between the approximate posterior q(z|x) and the true posterior p(z|x).

nodes.text: The ELBO of a VAE decomposes into a reconstruction term E[log p(x|z)] and a prior matching term -KL(q(z|x)||p(z)); the latter is computed analytically for Gaussian encoder/prior and the former via Monte Carlo.
nodes.evidence: reconstruction term ... prior matching term ... the KL divergence term of the ELBO can be computed analytically, and the reconstruction term can be approximated using a Monte Carlo estimate.

nodes.text: The reparameterization trick rewrites a sampled latent as a deterministic function of input and auxiliary noise (z = mu_phi(x) + sigma_phi(x) epsilon), enabling gradient-based optimization through the otherwise non-differentiable stochastic sampling step.
nodes.evidence: The reparameterization trick rewrites a random variable as a deterministic function of a noise variable; this allows for the optimization of the non-stochastic terms through gradient descent.

nodes.text: A Hierarchical VAE generalizes the VAE to multiple latent hierarchies; the Markovian HVAE (MHVAE) restricts the generative process to a Markov chain where each latent zt is generated only from zt+1, equivalent to stacking VAEs.
nodes.evidence: In a MHVAE, the generative process is a Markov chain; that is, each transition down the hierarchy is Markovian

nodes.text: Diffusion models admit three equivalent interpretations of what the neural network can be trained to predict (the original source image x0, the source noise, and the score of the data at each noise level).

Score-based generative models are highly related to diffusion models: rather than learning the energy function itself, they learn the score (gradient of log density) of an energy-based model as a neural network.
nodes.evidence: instead of learning to model the energy function itself, they learn the score of the energy-based model as a neural network.

nodes.text: The ELBO is derived two ways: via Jensen's inequality (which obscures why it is a lower bound) and via the chain rule (which reveals the gap is exactly the non-negative KL between approximate and true posterior).
nodes.evidence: it was this KL Divergence term that was magically removed by Jensen's Inequality in Equation 8 of the first derivation.

nodes.text: The review covers both classifier guidance and classifier-free guidance as techniques for controlling diffusion model generation.
Maximizing the ELBO serves a dual purpose: it acts as a proxy for matching the true posterior and, once trained, the ELBO can be used to estimate the likelihood of observed or generated data.
nodes.evidence: once trained, the ELBO can be used to estimate the likelihood of observed or generated data as well, since it is learned to approximate the model evidence log p(x).
